types.name: CartChatLookup
types.description:
Simple lookup object, this will provide ids and access creds if needed too. This represents several intersection of states where the user may have potential access to the cart.

1. User is authed and has ownership of the cart: Just a cartId will be provided. The client can continue interacting without any special actions.
2. User is authed, but does not own the cart and no one else owns the cart. chatLookupToken will be provided. Claim the cart immediately in this case so that it can be merged with the current user's cart.
3. User is authed but someone else owns this cart: needsImmediateLogin will be set to true. Prompt the user to log into the correct account linked with the user.
4. User is not authed and someone else owns this cart: needsImmediateLogin will be set to true. The correct user must be logged into to continue.
5. User is not authed and no one else owns the cart: Use cartId and chatLookupToken until checkout, then force the user to login and run claimCart using the cartId and cartLookupToken

fields.name: cartId
fields.description: The cart id the original lookup token is for. This will be needed for cart crud operations if the `chatLookupToken` is also set or `ownsCart` is set to `false`

fields.name: chatLookupToken
fields.description:
This is provided if the current client is not authed, but they can act in an unauthed fashion on the cart until the last moment. This is most likely going to be the most common flow. Use this token to do crud operations when the argument specifies it.

**NOTE: This expires after an hour, refresh this token every so often.**

fields.name: needsImmediateLogin
fields.description: This means that a cart is attached to the credentials provided, but you are either logged into another user other than the one referrer link expects (ex: The facebook user expected for the cart is not attached to the currently authed user). Orrrr the client is not logged in but not to the correct account. To protect that user's privacy they need to auth immediately.

fields.name: ownsCart
fields.description: Cart is owned by user. You do not need to do anything special when this is true

fields.name: sellerId
fields.description: This means the client is coming from a simulcast display **ONLY** that seller's storefront and filter the cart and checkout by this sellerId

fields.name: simulcastInstanceId
fields.description: The simulcast instance referrer, this is unused anywhere at the moment but will eventually become relavent during checkout.

fields.name: streamId
fields.description: This means the client is coming from a simulcast display too. This hints at the client to show this stream's information.

fields.name: hash
fields.description:
A hash of the current state of the cart. This is very useful for a checkout
                    flow where you want the drip prepurchase screen to the vendor purchase screen
                    to match exactly. Carts otherwise can occassionaly drift state if quantity or
                    pricing change in the interim.

                    This also prevents a seller changing an item to a new title or description
                    without the user discovering first.

                    If a flash sale has ended or changed price, this will also help.

                    You can pass this along with the cart id to the create payment apis and it will
                    return an error if the new cart hash doesn't match.

                    NOTE: this query is also expensive. This should only be queryed when needed.

fields.description: Will not exist if the cart is not valid

types.name: CartLookupInput
types.description:
Formalized lookup for a cart. A cart can be looked up a bunch of different ways. The client's identity determines which arguments it can use.
For external clients, you only need to pay attention to cartId and cartKey as those can lookup a cart from an unauthed context. Other methods include looking
up by some external account ids. This simplifies other services not having to manage the tricky bits of cart ownership. Leave arguments null if you do not
want to look up by them. You can only look up by one method. Others will get overridden. The order of precendence is as follows:

1. cartId/cartKey
2. userId
3. externalIds such as facebookUserId or twitchUserId

inputFields.name: cartId
inputFields.description: Look up the cart directly, provide the cart key if you are from an external client too.

inputFields.name: cartKey
inputFields.description:
This key is used for claiming a cart and operating on a cart from an external client. Drip does not store this code, only a hash. So if
this is lost, the cart is inaccessible.

This is removed once the cart is claimed by a user too.

This is unneeded if client has elevated permissions (admin or trusted service), but still can be set if needed to replicate permission structure.

inputFields.name: chatLookupToken
inputFields.description:
This token is a short lived token that can be used to also access the cart. This requires also providing the cart id too.

You can get this from the cartChatLookup. It's really only meant to be used with the chat bot.

inputFields.name: facebookUserId
inputFields.description:
Look up by facebookUserId. This will return a user's cart if the facebookUser is linked to one, otherwise an anonymous cart. Be careful with that implication.

This is only available to admins and privileged services.

inputFields.name: twitchUserId
inputFields.description:
Look up by twitchUserId. This will return a user's cart if the twitchUser is linked to one, otherwise an anonymous cart. Be careful with that implication.

This is only available to admins and privileged services.

inputFields.name: userId
inputFields.description: Look up by a userId. This is only available to admins and privileged services.

types.name: OAuthCartJoinInfo
types.description:
Info around joining drip/connecting an account to drip that will have a cart item auto added. The main purpose of this is for environments where we will send someone that has potentially not authed with Drip to join and get a cart seeded with an item.

When this is employed, the backend has literally no idea about the user when a link is generated. This data encapsulates the several states that can occur once a client has followed the link and sent it back to us with any potential auth info attached.

These are:

  1. User is authed, but potentially has not authed with this link. You could compare if the product id returned and optional simulcast instance id match anything in their current cart
  2. User is authed and someone has authed with this id, this data is temporary and disappears after several months, but we will check to see if this oauth link had someone connect an account with it, along with seeing if that account was attached to this user. The client can decide with the data provided whether to roll the dice and just forward the user directly to the cart.
  3. No one is logged in. Use the data provided to display the appropriate oauth link

types.name: __Directive
types.description:
A Directive provides a way to describe alternate runtime execution and type validation behavior in a GraphQL document.

In some cases, you need to provide options to alter GraphQL's execution behavior in ways field arguments will not suffice, such as conditionally including or skipping a field. Directives provide this by describing additional information to the executor.

types.name: __DirectiveLocation
types.description: A Directive can be adjacent to many parts of the GraphQL language, a __DirectiveLocation describes one such possible adjacencies.

enumValues.name: QUERY
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a query operation.

enumValues.name: MUTATION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a mutation operation.

enumValues.name: SUBSCRIPTION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a subscription operation.

enumValues.name: FIELD
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a field.

enumValues.name: FRAGMENT_DEFINITION

enumValues.name: FRAGMENT_SPREAD
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a fragment spread.

enumValues.name: INLINE_FRAGMENT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an inline fragment.

enumValues.name: VARIABLE_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a variable definition.

enumValues.name: SCHEMA
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a schema definition.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a scalar definition.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an object type definition.

enumValues.name: FIELD_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a field definition.

enumValues.name: ARGUMENT_DEFINITION

enumValues.name: INTERFACE

enumValues.name: ENUM

types.description: A GraphQL Schema defines the capabilities of a GraphQL server. It exposes all available types and directives on the server, as well as the entry points for query, mutation, and subscription operations.

types.name: __Type
types.description:
The fundamental unit of any GraphQL Schema is the type. There are many kinds of types in GraphQL as represented by the `__TypeKind` enum.

Depending on the kind of a type, certain fields describe information about that type. Scalar types provide no information beyond a name, description and optional `specifiedByURL`, while Enum types provide their values. Object and Interface types provide the fields they describe. Abstract types, Union and Interface, provide the Object types possible at runtime. List and NonNull types compose other types.

types.name: __TypeKind
types.description: An enum describing what kind of type a given `__Type` is.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a scalar.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an object. `fields` and `interfaces` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an interface. `fields`, `interfaces`, and `possibleTypes` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a union. `possibleTypes` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an enum. `enumValues` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an input object. `inputFields` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: LIST
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a list. `ofType` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: NON_NULL
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a non-null. `ofType` is a valid field.
